small_guidance:
- The GEMM is M=N=K=8192 — add larger tile configs (BLOCK_M=128/BLOCK_N=256/BLOCK_K=64 num_warps=8 num_stages=3-4, and BLOCK_M=256/BLOCK_N=128/BLOCK_K=32) and consider dropping the K-mask in the inner loop since K is a multiple of BLOCK_K (K=8192) to remove per-iteration mask overhead.
- Tune softmax: try BLOCK_N=4096 with num_warps=8 and num_stages=2; the current BLOCK_N=8192 + num_warps=16 may spill. Also consider a two-pass softmax that re-reads from the (cached) GEMM output rather than the single-pass-then-rewrite pattern.
- Consider fusing the row-max/row-sum partial reduction of softmax directly into the GEMM epilogue (compute per-tile max and sumexp atomically into per-row scratch), eliminating one full read of the 1024×8192 tensor.
large_guidance:
- Replace the two-kernel pipeline with a fused GEMM+softmax persistent kernel: each program owns a row tile of M and streams across all N tiles, accumulating GEMM output into SMEM/registers and performing online softmax in the same kernel so the 32 MB intermediate is never written to HBM. With M=1024 and N=8192 this is the dominant memory cost.
- Alternatively, split into a "GEMM + per-row partial max/sumexp" kernel (writes y plus two M-length reduction tensors), then a tiny normalize kernel — this avoids the second full HBM read in the current softmax. Use atomic max + atomic add into per-row scratch, or one program per row group.
- For the GEMM itself, try a split-K variant (K=8192 is large) with atomic add into the output, or use tf32/`tl.dot(..., allow_tf32=True)` to nearly double throughput; the reference BN+softmax tolerates the lower precision under atol=5e-2.
